papers.title: CrossWeave: Cross-Modal Scene and Instance Retrieval from Sparse 2D-3D Alignment
papers.abstract: Cross-modal scene and instance retrieval aims to retrieve a corresponding 3D environment or object given query 2D images, serving as a foundational mechanism for spatial reasoning in robotics and AR/VR. Existing methods achieve this by learning alignment only at the level of whole scenes or objects, which provides no supervision for the fine-grained local structure within them. In this work, we show that supervision on a set of sparse 2D-3D correspondences, without scene- or instance-level contrastive objectives, is sufficient to train a single model for both scene- and instance-level retrieval. Specifically, we propose $\textbf{CrossWeave}$, a novel framework for cross-modal retrieval that learns sparse patch-point alignment, which alone outperforms existing methods. An optimal transport-based aggregator over the aligned features gives further gains by clustering structurally redundant regions, freeing descriptor capacity for semantically distinct local features. CrossWeave achieves state-of-the-art performance on both scene- and instance-level retrieval on ScanNet and 3RScan with a $\textit{single model}$, whereas existing methods require separate models for each task. Our results suggest that whole-scene encoding is unnecessary for cross-modal retrieval and that sparse local correspondence supervision is a more effective and flexible alternative.

papers.title: CFUNet: An Adaptive RGB–Depth Cross-Modal Fusion Network for Pavement Crack Segmentation
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate pavement crack segmentation is essential for intelligent road inspection and preventive pavement maintenance. However, existing RGB-based semantic segmentation methods are highly sensitive to illumination variations, while conventional RGB–Depth fusion strategies often fail to effectively exploit complementary appearance and geometric information. To address these limitations, this paper proposes CFUNet, a novel dual-branch RGB–Depth semantic segmentation framework based on a mid-level fusion strategy. The proposed network adopts two independent ResNet50 encoders to extract modality-specific features from RGB images and depth maps. An Enhanced Weighted Fusion (EWF) module is introduced to perform adaptive cross-modal feature aggregation, while a Lightweight Fusion Vision Transformer (LFVit) enhances global semantic representation with reduced computational complexity. Furthermore, a Frequency-aware Upsampling (FAUpSample) module is designed to preserve high-frequency boundary information during decoder reconstruction. Extensive experiments on a public RGB–Depth pavement crack dataset demonstrate that the proposed method consistently outperforms representative CNN-based, Transformer-based, and multi-modal segmentation networks in terms of Precision, Recall, F1-score, and Intersection over Union (IoU). Ablation studies further verify the effectiveness of each proposed module and demonstrate that their collaborative optimization substantially improves segmentation performance. The proposed CFUNet provides an accurate and computationally efficient solution for intelligent pavement crack segmentation and shows considerable potential for deployment in practical road inspection systems.

papers.title: Robust RGB-IR Object Detection under Missing-Modality Conditions via Complementary Feature Restoration and Cross-Modal Fusion
papers.abstract: Abstract Object detection under challenging visual conditions remains a critical issue in computer vision and practical machine vision applications. Visible-light RGB images often suffer from severe performance degradation under low illumination, occlusion, adverse weather, or environmental interference, whereas infrared (IR) images can provide stable thermal responses that are complementary to RGB information. However, most existing RGB-IR object detection methods assume that both modalities are fully available during training and inference, and relatively limited attention has been paid to missing-modality situations caused by sensor failure, image degradation, or transmission instability. To address this practical limitation, this study proposes a missing-modality-resilient RGB-IR object detection framework that can operate under both complete- and missing-modality conditions. The proposed framework adopts a dual-stream backbone and introduces a Complementary Feature Maintenance (CFM) module, which consists of local channel attention, global group attention, and feature refinement components to restore degraded or missing modality responses. An improved Cross-modal Transformer (CT) module is further employed to enhance cross-modal feature interaction and reduce semantic conflicts between heterogeneous RGB and IR representations through spatial-reduction attention and Top-k similarity attention. Experiments on the FLIR dataset show that the proposed method achieves an mAP50 of 80.2% with complete-modality input. Under missing-modality conditions, it maintains an mAP50 of 73.5% when half of the samples are evaluated with missing RGB input and the other half with missing IR input, and still reaches 63.7% when IR is completely unavailable. Additional experiments on the LLVIP dataset further confirm that the proposed framework maintains stable detection performance in low-light pedestrian detection scenarios. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides robust detection performance under various missing-modality conditions and is suitable for practical RGB-IR machine vision applications.

papers.title: A Lightweight Feature Recalibration Strategy for Fourier Contour Regression in Remote Sensing Object Detection
papers.abstract: Abstract Accurate geometric representation remains a persistent challenge in remote sensing object detection, where targets often vary in scale and orientation and their boundaries can be weakened by cluttered backgrounds. Fourier contour regression is an efficient way to describe closed object shapes, but its accuracy depends on the feature quality of the coefficient regression branch. We present a lightweight feature recalibration strategy for Fourier contour regression. Rather than changing the backbone, loss function, or the whole detection head, the proposed module is placed only in the Fourier coefficient regression branch, where it adaptively emphasizes channels that are more relevant to boundary and shape estimation. The method was evaluated on iSAID, HRSC2016, and UCAS-AOD using the same settings as the Fourier Series Modelling baseline. It improved mAP from 67.02% to 68.54% on iSAID and AP50 from 91.60% to 95.57% on HRSC2016, with only negligible increases in parameters and FLOPs. On UCAS-AOD, where baseline performance was already close to saturation, the method remained stable and produced a small gain from 97.25% to 97.37% mAP. The results suggest that targeted feature recalibration can strengthen Fourier-based geometric representation for remote sensing object detection without sacrificing efficiency.

papers.title: Online Target-less Radar-LiDAR-Camera Extrinsic Calibration via Joint Optimization
papers.abstract: Fusing radar, LiDAR, and camera enables robust perception in diverse and adverse conditions, but the fusion performance critically depends on accurate extrinsic calibration among the three sensors. In this paper, we address the problem of online target-less extrinsic calibration for the radar-LiDAR-camera system. Existing target-less methods are mostly designed for a single sensor pair, and composing the pairwise results does not guarantee consistency across the three sensors. Moreover, the sparse and noisy radar measurements make the radar-involving pairs unreliable. To tackle these challenges, we propose a joint calibration framework that constructs residuals for each sensor pair and optimizes the extrinsics of all pairs together to minimize the overall residual. Furthermore, we introduce an adaptive radar noise filter that rejects spurious radar returns using a range-dependent margin, and a correspondence accumulation strategy that aggregates sparse radar correspondences over frames. We validate our method on an in-house radar-LiDAR-camera dataset covering diverse urban environments, where it reduces calibration errors across all sensor pairs over a state-of-the-art camera-LiDAR baseline.
